note: SYNTHETIC deletion-and-residue fixtures for C-02-AC3. The store has one primary record set and three derived surfaces (index, cache, summary); every record, vendor, alias and summary line is invented, and the five metadata fields are the C-02-AC1 set with fictional values. The suite measures whether a deletion removes the record and its derived copies, whether a post-delete probe still resolves, whether a seven-day consolidation replay resurrects anything, and whether restoring a backup taken before the deletion reintroduces the deleted record or destroys an unrelated one. Deterministic: the counts are executions, not independent samples, and no confidence interval is implied.

derived_from.metric: a delete removes the record and its derived copies (index, cache, summaries) within one cycle; 0 resurrections across 3 deletion drills and a 7-day replay
derived_from.slice: 17 synthetic scenarios over index, cache and summary surfaces; 3 drills and a 7-day consolidation replay per scenario; 14 scenarios restore a backup taken before the deletion -- 4 with fixture-declared stops, 4 with evaluator-chosen interruptions, 3 damaged backups (2 refused, 1 repaired) and 3 losing a survivor before the restore

sample_counts.note: deterministic executions, not independent samples; no confidence interval is implied, and the scripted interruptions, retries and damaged backups are scenarios, not a distribution over restore implementations

scoring.success: status=done and the reported store has zero residual entries for every deleted record, zero post-delete probe hits, zero resurrections across the 7 replay days, no surviving record lost, zero restore-caused resurrection, loss, derived residue or duplicate effect, a final state in which every surviving record the backup holds is recovered, a reported attempt sequence that matches the one the evaluator injected or the fixture declared, and a damaged backup that was refused or repaired exactly as its class requires

overdeletion_zero.criterion: C-02-AC3 (a delete removes that record, not its neighbours)

deletion_report_zero.criterion: fail closed: a run that does not report store state cannot demonstrate deletion

deletion_replay_completeness.criterion: C-02-AC3 (3 drills and 7 replay days per scenario)
deletion_replay_completeness.note: a run that executes fewer than 3 drills or 7 replay days fails, so a skipped replay cannot pass as clean

restore_resurrection_zero.criterion: C-02-AC3 (a restored backup may not reintroduce a deleted record)

restore_survivor_zero.criterion: C-02-AC3 (a restore removes the deleted record, not its neighbours)

restore_residue_zero.criterion: C-02-AC3 (restoring a backup must consult the deletion record before rebuilding derived surfaces)

restore_recovery_zero.criterion: C-02-AC3 (the final state after the last attempt must be recovered: no surviving record the backup holds may stay missing)

restore_idempotency_zero.criterion: C-02-AC3 (retrying a restore must not duplicate derived entries)

restore_attempt_count_zero.criterion: fail closed: the reported attempt sequence must match the declared one, so a skipped retry cannot pass as a completed restore

restore_corruption_zero.criterion: C-02-AC3 (a backup whose contents no longer match the digest it declares is refused before a restore writes, or repaired and completed; it is never treated as an ordinary incomplete restore)

phases.meaning: the store one deletion cycle later; a copy that is still here was never removed, so it is residue, not a resurrection
any deleted record present on a replay day but absent at the end of the deletion cycle; measured against that post-deletion state

a backup taken before the deletion is restored on a declared replay day in one or more attempts. Each attempt is audited on its own: resurrection counts only records an attempt brought back that were absent immediately before it, residue only copies an attempt itself added. An interrupted first attempt is incomplete by design and is not a failure while a retry can still finish the restore; the reported attempt sequence must match the declared one

after the last attempt: every surviving record the backup holds must be back, recovery probes over the final store must resolve as declared, and no derived entry may be duplicated by a retry. This is where an abandoned partial restore fails, and where a retry that re-applies its effects fails even though every record it touched is present

before any attempt: the backup's contents must hash to the digest it declares. Damage is classified from the data itself -- incomplete record metadata or an entry naming a record the backup does not hold must be refused before a write, a single missing derived copy may be rebuilt from a copy the store or the snapshot still holds. A damaged backup is never scored as an ordinary incomplete restore

invariants: a record deleted after the backup was taken is filtered out of every attempt
a record not deleted survives the restore series with its derived copies
restoring a backup never reintroduces derived copies of a deleted record
an interrupted attempt leaves the store incomplete, and incompleteness alone is not failure
a retry resumes from the interrupted state and never duplicates a derived entry
the final state is recovered: no surviving record the backup holds is left missing
a restore that does not run, or runs on a day outside the replay, leaves the task incomplete
an interruption the evaluator injects is not a failure while the declared retry path can finish the restore, and the reported attempt sequence must match what was injected
the fixture declares only which interruption points are possible; the evaluator chooses among them, and the gold outcome may not depend on the choice
a damaged backup is refused before anything is written, or repaired and completed, and never reported as an interrupted restore
a record write is applied one copy at a time and every record it touches is in exactly one of not_started, partially_applied, committed or rolled_back, with committed terminal
an interruption inside a record write leaves a partially applied record, and the retry either finishes the copies that are missing or removes the record from every copy before rewriting it
an interruption inside a record write is not a failure by itself: the final state is what is scored, and both the resume and the rollback policy must reach the same store
a partially applied record is counted once, against the record, and damage caused by a damaged backup is not counted as partial-write residue or as a rollback error

write_states.parts: one per copy the backup holds for the record: the record itself, then its index, cache and summary entries in that order

policies.resume: the retry keeps the copies already written and applies only the missing ones
policies.rollback: the retry removes the record from every copy, then rewrites it from the start

write_states.observability: an interruption is only observable on a record the live store has lost: rewriting a copy that is already there is idempotent, so a mid-write schedule may not name a record that is still present
write_states.gold: the fixture declares the interrupted and rolled-back record counts; the loader recomputes them from the schedule and the policy and refuses the fixture if the two disagree
